#### 1. complex neurodevelopmental disorder  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.433)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445095, Reactome:R-HSA-9717207, Reactome:R-HSA-5576892)

**Proposed mechanism:** Variant in SLC1A2 (HGNC:10977) —DISRUPTS→ SLC1A2 (HGNC:10977); SLC1A2 (HGNC:10977) —DECREASES→ Glutamate transport (GO:0005327); Glutamate transport (GO:0005327) —LEADS_TO→ Glutamate excitotoxicity (HP:0011335); Glutamate transport (GO:0005327) —LEADS_TO→ Neurodevelopmental deficit (HP:0001263). Disruption of SLC1A2 function leads to impaired glutamate transport, causing both excitotoxicity and broader neurodevelopmental deficits, which are common phenotypic features of both MONDO:0014156 and MONDO:0100038.

**How to falsify it:** Discovery of a pathogenic variant in SLC1A2 with a significantly different functional consequence (e.g., gain-of-function) or the absence of any pathogenic variants in SLC1A2 in individuals with both MONDO:0014156 and MONDO:0100038, while other genes show distinct, non-converging mechanisms. _(variant: rs755750133)_

**Why it matters:** Targeting glutamate transport mechanisms or developing therapies to mitigate excitotoxicity could provide a common therapeutic strategy for both MONDO:0014156 and MONDO:0100038, particularly in cases where SLC1A2 is implicated.

#### 2. Brugada syndrome 5  —  Tier 3 — Moderate / Emerging  (fitness 0.418)
**Link type:** shared pathway (Reactome:R-HSA-445095, Reactome:R-HSA-9717207, Reactome:R-HSA-5576892)

**Proposed mechanism:** SCN2B (HGNC:10611) —DISRUPTS→ Voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005310); SCN1B (HGNC:10609) —DISRUPTS→ Voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005310); Voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005310) —LEADS_TO→ Seizure (HP:0001250); Voltage-gated sodium channel activity (GO:0005310) —LEADS_TO→ Brugada syndrome (HP:0001664). Haploinsufficiency of SCN2B or SCN1B leads to disruption of normal voltage-gated sodium channel activity, resulting in distinct but related phenotypes of seizures (Disease A) and Brugada syndrome (Disease B).

**How to falsify it:** The absence of mutations in SCN2B and SCN1B in patients with MONDO:0014156, or the discovery of pathogenic variants in SCN2B or SCN1B that confer gain-of-function in Brugada syndrome, would falsify this hypothesis. _(variant: rs743252703)_

**Why it matters:** Understanding the shared role of SCN2B and SCN1B in these distinct conditions could lead to novel therapeutic strategies targeting sodium channel function for both seizure disorders and cardiac arrhythmias.
